fixes.explanation: The army is the one marching, so that guess makes sense. But Moses doesn't call it theirs. He says they are to "…execute the LORD’s vengeance on them." (Numbers 31:3) The vengeance is called the LORD's, friend, and that's the word to hold onto.

False is right! The army carried away "…all the plunder and spoils, both people and animals." (Numbers 31:11) And they brought "…the captives, spoils, and plunder…" to Moses, Eleazar the priest, and the congregation. (Numbers 31:12) The plunder came to the camp right along with the captives.

That's the one! Moses asks the officers, "Have you spared all the women?" (Numbers 31:15) He's angry when he asks it, and the very next verse is where he explains himself. I think that's a question nobody wants to hear from an angry boss.

Balak son of Zippor is a name from Balaam's story, so I get why it came to mind. But Moses doesn't name him here. He says it was "…through the counsel of Balaam…" (Numbers 31:16) That's Balaam son of Beor, and he's the one Moses names.

Og king of Bashan is a name from Israel's travels, but he isn't in this verse. Moses says the women caused it "…through the counsel of Balaam…" (Numbers 31:16) So the answer is Balaam son of Beor. Og can sit this one out.

Right, the "congregation." The LORD says to "…divide the captives between the troops who went out to battle and the rest of the congregation." (Numbers 31:27) Two shares, one for the soldiers and one for everybody else. That's a clean split, and the LORD is the one who laid it out.

Not quite, friend. The commanders say, "Your servants have counted the soldiers under our command, and not one of us is missing." (Numbers 31:49) Nobody is missing in their report, so the answer is False.

False is right! The commanders say, "…not one of us is missing." (Numbers 31:49) They counted the soldiers under their command and reported nobody missing. I'd have counted twice and still been nervous.

Mount Nebo is a mountain, so I see where that came from. But in this verse, they brought the gold "…into the Tent of Meeting as a memorial for the Israelites before the LORD." (Numbers 31:54) The gold went into the Tent of Meeting, not up a mountain. No hiking boots needed.
